findings.reason: the plan should state which of `machine.py`'s owner classes it extends (and whether a new section model is genuinely needed for winding sections) instead of proposing an ITER conductor build without naming the existing ITER conductor builder.
findings.text: the plan builds the sectioned ITER conductor set from `ITER_MACHINE_DESCRIPTION/3/111001` run 204 without citing the module that already reads exactly that: `nova/imas/machine.py` defines `Machine`, `Geometry` (with `pf_active`/`pf_passive`/`wall` fields, lines 1423–1497), `PoloidalFieldActive` (line 1032), `PoloidalFieldPassive` (line 965), `Wall` (line 1207), `IdsCoilData`/`ActiveCoilData`/`PassiveShellData` (lines 751–1030), `Loop`/`ActiveLoop`/`Element` (lines 568–642) and the machine-description record seam `StaticMachineDescription`/`MachineCoil`/`MachineSection`/`MachineCoil`/`ImasGeometryReader`/`TabularGeometryReader`/`CrossSection` (lines 270–566); `nova/imas/pulsedesign.py:26` defines `ITER(Machine)` with `pf_active="iter_md"`, `pf_passive="iter_md"`; `nova/imas/transient.py:15` defines `Transient(Machine)` with the same defaults. The plan's §1 concept of a coil "section" (double pancake, CS pancake) is a second section model beside `machine.py`'s `MachineSection`/`CrossSection`.

findings.reason: naming `PF_Passive` as the comparison-source owner removes a re-implementation of that reader and fixes the group mapping the done-when depends on.
findings.text: §3 compares the evolved passive currents "group by group with DINA's own `pf_passive` currents", but the mechanism that reads and groups DINA's `pf_passive` loop currents already exists as `PF_Passive(Plot, Scenario)` (`name = "pf_passive"`, `ids_node = "loop"`, `loop_attrs = ["current"]`), and `nova/imas/machine.py:965` `PoloidalFieldPassive` builds the passive geometry from the same IDS; the plan names neither file.

findings.reason: §2's "build the distribution" step is largely `Profile.j_tor_rbs`; the plan should extend it rather than re-derive j_φ, and say so.
findings.text: §2 step 2 evaluates `j_φ(R,Z) = R p′(ψ) + FF′(ψ)/(μ0 R)` on nova's plasma grid from DINA's 1-D flux functions and its 2-D ψ map, but `nova/imas/profiles.py` already implements this: `Profile.fluxfunctions` (line 57) with the `p_prime`/`ff_prime` branch, `Profile.j_tor_rbs` (line 87), `Profile._rbs` (line 96) and `Profile.delaunay` (line 92). The plan cites `nova/imas/equilibrium.py` and `nova/imas/extrapolate.py` but not the module that owns the flux-function-to-current-density evaluation.

findings.reason: the section must say whether the new export replaces the existing `PassiveStructure`/`matrices.json` representation or adds beside it, or the converter model will carry two divergent passive models.
findings.text: §4 exports "the reduced passive system: the eigenmodes kept, their decay times and their coupling to every coil section" over the machine description, but the consumer already owns a reduced passive representation that reads the same source: `PassiveStructure` (filament inductance/mutual/resistance/group, source recorded in `data/iter/passive_structure/matrices.json` as `/work/imas/shared/imasdb/ITER_MACHINE_DESCRIPTION/3/111001/204/pf_active; .../115004/6/pf_passive; .../124001/3/pf_passive`), reduced by `power_convertor/src/power_convertor/passive_structure.py` and consumed by `coupled_circuit.py:31`. §4 adds a parallel versioned file without naming that this representation is being superseded (the plan's own premise is that the existing ring model is invalid above 1.8/29–35 Hz).

findings.reason: extending the existing serialiser is the honest change; a parallel loader is surface without depth unless the record shape genuinely cannot fit the existing contract.
findings.text: §4's "round-trip test of the loader passes in nova" presupposes a new file contract plus a new nova loader, but the serialisation owner `nova/circuit/passive.py` already ships `save_circuit_system`/`load_circuit_system` (lines 570, 591) and `save_eigenbasis`/`load_eigenbasis` (lines 615, 633) for a `PassiveCircuitSystem`/`PassiveEigenbasis`, and `nova/circuit/screening.py` already exports `CoupledCircuit`. The plan does not say why the coupled plant cannot ride the existing circuit-system serialiser.

findings.reason: the export path should resolve through the project's `FilePath`/repository-relative mechanism so the artefact is discoverable and the receipt survives a checkout move.
findings.text: §4 hard-codes the absolute destination `/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/power_convertor/data/iter/coupled_plant/`, while path resolution is owned by `nova/database/filepath.py` (`class FilePath`, line 358: `path`/`resolve`/`file`, and the repository-relative helpers `repository_relative` line 279 / `relativize_worktree_paths` line 74). A literal absolute path into a sibling repository both bypasses that owner and re-introduces a machine-local path the repo's own pre-commit hook (`scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit`, `filepath relativize --check`) is built to keep out of tracked files.

findings.reason: the section must name what the new contract/loader retires (the existing `PassiveStructure` representation and `save_circuit_system`/`load_circuit_system`) or state why nothing can be.
findings.text: §4 states "The contract is written down in the record", adding a new public loader and a new versioned file contract, and neither §4 nor §1's added conductor-set builder names a definition it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be; measured against this week's figures (public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0) the plan adds public-definition surface with no accounting in its own text.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the core of the plan extends existing deep modules (`PassiveCircuit`, `integrate_eddy_ode`, `circuit_linkage_matrix`); §4 adds one export artefact plus its loader rather than a spread of wrappers.

rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §4 adds a new public loader and versioned file contract without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites `nova/circuit/{passive,propagate,linkage,screening}.py` and `nova/imas/{equilibrium,extrapolate}.py`, but the machinery it rebuilds is already owned by `nova/imas/machine.py`, `nova/imas/pf_passive.py`, `nova/imas/profiles.py` and `power_convertor/src/power_convertor/passive_structure.py`, none of which it names.
